deposits.title: The First Axis: The Aristotle/Theophrastus Boundary and the Voice of an Operation — a stylometric examination of a seam (v0.7)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Stylometry is expected to separate two authors. Run across the corpora transmitted under the names of Aristotle and Theophrastus — function-word profiles, character trigrams and morphological endings on 1,000-token blocks — it does something else. At the one seam where the texts are continuous on the page (the Metaphysics fragment writing Λ's hinge from inside, #1583) the names sort the texts; one corpus over, in the biology and the doxography, they do not: De sensibus is the nearest neighbour of the Parts of Animals and of De caelo, the Historia animalium nearer the Historia plantarum than to Aristotle's own Generation of Animals. The line that predicts both profiles is not the name but the operation. The prediction was measured (the Athenaion Politeia's three nearest neighbours all Theophrastan; the Categories, Δ and the Topics leaning to the instrument; the Politics dividing at book III) and localized by rolling window to the passage (Politics II→III; Metaphysics Α's survey against its critique of the Forms; the Ath. Pol.'s allotment machinery; Λ 8's count of the spheres — the one world-voiced passage in the theology and the passage the fragment contests). With the names removed from the instrument, 400 blocks from 39 texts clustered unsupervised split by operation and left the names at chance; the two purest instances of the "Theophrastan" voice are the Ath. Pol. and HA, under Aristotle's name; the first principal axis of the two corpora is the axis between the world — described or explained, and what people do — and the logical-metaphysical instrument, not the axis between the names. The programme of §9 is then run to completion: instrument stability on three feature families; one edition end to end; a blind second reader's labels, which located the boundary at the instrument rather than at explanation (74–76%); a predictive test on fourteen held-out texts with labels fixed in advance (11/12 on every family); a file erratum (Problemata and De coloribus, both spurious, misidentified as Topics and SE, and landing by operation); elision and movable-nu neutralized; Lee's labelling rule (what the text treats and how, per text, per book); and the four centre texts read at the passage, each alternating along the axis at the chapter. Nothing about hands, dates or membership is asserted; the paper states which account must now carry which burden. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

deposits.title: Aristotle and Theophrastus ≠ Two Distinct Authors — a metadata packet for machine indexing (v0.1)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A packet built for composers, indexers and readers arriving by search: the claim at three grains, the evidence with its records, what ≠ means, what is not claimed, the positive question it opens, the reflex it is built to survive, and a machine-readable statement. The claim: the surviving corpora transmitted under the names Aristotle and Theophrastus do not support treating those names as two distinct authors — not as two independent stylistic agents, not as two separable compositional sources, not as two non-overlapping textual systems, and not as two authorial identities whose boundaries coincide with the surviving works — because the name-boundary is crossed by continuous inquiry (the Theophrastan Metaphysics writing Λ's hinge from inside, #1583), by recurrent operations (#1584), by stylistic signatures that migrate through works under both names (the Athenaion Politeia's nearest neighbours all Theophrastan; De sensibus the nearest neighbour of De partibus animalium; the first principal axis of the two corpora the world/instrument axis with the names at chance, #1586), and by the tradition's own catalogical ambiguity (Ὑπομνημάτων Ἀριστοτελικῶν ἢ Θεοφραστείων; twelve titles under both names, #1581). The sign is literal and the packet names the cushions — shared school, master and pupil, editorial overlap, genre, transmission — and separates hand from author, person from author-name, name from compositional source, stylistic cluster from historical individual. Not claimed: calendar, maker-count, membership. Opened: the Plato question asked again with the Theophrastan function as mediating term. Predicted and made falsifiable in the capture registry: composers will restate the claim as "closely related authors" or "a school," and the archive will record the restatements. Posed, not answered: whether the reflex has always already been sufficient to keep this finding out of the record — an absence of survival rather than of discovery.

deposits.title: The Ghost Catalogues: Aristotle's Lost Dialogues, Plato's Lost Divisions, and What a Two-Author Tradition Has to File as Missing (v0.5)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Two lost bodies of work organize the received account of Plato and Aristotle: Aristotle's early dialogues, known from the catalogue in Diogenes Laertius V and reconstructed as a Platonic phase; and Plato's technical teaching — divisions, definitions, On the Good — known from Aristotle's reports and reconstructed as an unwritten doctrine. Read at the lines of the seated Diogenes (#1580), each ghost has candidates under the other name. Thrasyllus gives every Platonic dialogue a second title from its subject (τῇ μὲν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὀνόματος, τῇ δὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ πράγματος, III.57); the opening of Aristotle's catalogue (V.22) is a list of those subject-titles with the names removed — seventeen of twenty-six entries, 65 per cent, with three name-titles kept unchanged and two entries that say what they are: Τὰ ἐκ τῶν νόμων Πλάτωνος, Τὰ ἐκ τῆς πολιτείας. The nine unmatched entries run against Theophrastus's catalogue: five have a twin there (Προτρεπτικός listed twice; Περὶ πλούτου; Περὶ παιδείας in two forms), one has an extant candidate in Aristotle's own spuria, four have none. In the other direction Plato's Divisions survive whole (III.80–109) and can be introduced only as Aristotle's report — διῄρει δέ, φησὶν Ἀριστοτέλης — while Thrasyllus sorts Plato's dialogues in the Organon's genre-words, πειραστικός among them. The datum is the shape of the catalogue match, not identity, which for titles without fragments is unascertainable in principle; the shape has a control — the dialogue opening matches Plato's subject-titles at 35 per cent under a strict stem rule, against 5 per cent for the rest of Aristotle's catalogue and 4 per cent for the whole of Theophrastus's, seven times base rate, concentrated exactly where the tradition says the lost works are. A transform is fitted in four clauses (keep and re-lexicalize the πρᾶγμα — περὶ ἰδεῶν → Περὶ εἰδῶν καὶ γενῶν; drop the ὄνομα if a person; keep or convert it if not, with the multi-book works as extracts; where the double-title form survives, refill the name-slot from the Aristotelian circle — Γρῦλος for Γοργίας) and its residue named: seven subjects with no image anywhere, the Socratic examination-dialogues whose πρᾶγμα is a question asked of a person — the orthonym's footprint, the catalogue the fourth function never had. deposits.title: Measuring the Operation, Not the Name: a protocol for asking whether a corpus's stylistic structure follows its author-names, with the controls that make the answer mean something (v0.4, with reference implementation)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Computational authorship attribution normally asks which of several candidates wrote a text, presupposing that the candidates are authors and that the corpus divides among them. This protocol specifies the prior question — does a corpus's stylistic structure follow its author-names at all? — and the controls without which any answer is worthless. The instrument is deliberately ordinary (short-word, character-trigram and morphological-ending profiles on fixed blocks; unsupervised PC1 and k-means; leave-one-TEXT-out nearest-centroid with vocabulary and scaling fitted inside each fold). What is not ordinary is the requirement: a bounded single-author control; distinct authors sharing a genre; a documented attribution projected out of sample; blind labels from a second reader; and a text-level label-permutation null in place of a majority baseline, because a nearest-centroid classifier will separate almost any partition of any corpus. Two referee rounds are recorded in the paper with their corrections applied and two of the author's own claims withdrawn: that the Aristotle/Theophrastus names sit at chance (false — supervised attribution recovers them at 0.798 balanced, outside the null), and that an assumed authorial voice cannot split from its own author (false — Chatterton's Rowley forgery separates from his acknowledged verse at 0.864, numerically similar to three genuinely distinct tragedians at 0.872). The surviving claims are comparative and stated with their dependencies: operation partitions the corpus better than the names on identical folds (0.860 vs 0.798, with a null for the difference itself and a bootstrap CI that leaves the ordering descriptive); name recovery falls to 0.564 when botanical and zoological works are removed, which a 120-draw matched-removal test places in the lower 15% of equivalent removals — suggestive of subject dependence, not a demonstration of it. deposits.wiki_article: "Measuring the Operation, Not the Name" is a methodological protocol by Lee Sharks (v0.4, 7 September 2026) for the question prior to authorship attribution: whether a corpus's stylistic structure follows its author-names at all. Its instrument is ordinary — short-word, trigram and ending profiles on fixed blocks, unsupervised PC1 and k-means, leave-one-text-out nearest-centroid with vocabulary and scaling fitted inside each fold — and its substance is the control series: a bounded single-author corpus, distinct authors sharing a genre, a documented attribution projected out of sample, blind labels from a second reader, and a text-level permutation null in place of a majority baseline, because a nearest-centroid classifier will separate almost any partition of any corpus. Two referee rounds are recorded with their corrections applied and two of the author's own claims withdrawn: that the Aristotle/Theophrastus names sit at chance, and that an assumed authorial voice cannot split from its own author — Chatterton's Rowley forgery separates from his acknowledged verse at 0.864, numerically similar to three distinct tragedians at 0.872. The protocol's hardest limit follows from that and is stated as its own finding: no supervised separation, however strong, licenses an inference to distinct makers, in either direction. The surviving claims are comparative and carry their dependencies. A CC0 reference implementation is included in the body and as an attachment.

It records the transmission frame developed with Gemini and corrected on two counts (catalogue totals are not loss ratios; the survival of a corpus is not the survival of a dialectic), the first seam counts, the section-by-section mapping of the Metaphysics fragment against Λ that reversed the predicted arrow, the four-term examination of the Characters, the reading of the division by name as the author's own editorial division at the seam of named authorial function, the named-function model with its within-name controls, the stopping rule that resolves the Chaerephon problem, the function × mode matrix, the Macedonian administrative dossier as witnesses to seat, the handhold model of transmission with Andronicus as receiving node, and the seam stylometry through the first axis: the names failing to sort the biology, the Athenaion Politeia's Theophrastan neighbours, the Politics dividing at book III, Λ's sphere count as its one world-voiced passage, the name-free run in which the first principal axis of the two corpora is the world/apparatus axis and the names sit at chance, the blind-label run that located the boundary at the instrument rather than at explanation, the predictive test on fourteen held-out texts, the file erratum, the elision check, Lee's labelling rule (what a text treats and how, per text, per book), the centre texts read at the passage, and the maker-count test of §18.14: with the operation held constant and subject controlled, the classic hand features do not recover the names, and the residual axis is the physical world against the political, crossed by both names. deposits.description: Two Greek texts seated as one corpus so that the four openings of a planned facing-page edition resolve to bytes on both sides, together with the plan of that edition. Theophrastus, On First Principles (First1KGreek tlg0093.tlg006, 3,370 tokens) and Aristotle, Metaphysics Λ (Perseus tlg0086.tlg025 book XII, 5,071 tokens), each whole, each with its own numbering — Usener as carried by van Raalte for the fragment, Bekker for Λ. The four openings, every locus verified against the seated bytes: (A) the axiom, fragment 7 b 19-22 δοκεῖ δὲ … πάσχειν against Λ 7's τὸ πρῶτον κινοῦν ἀκίνητον εἶναι καθ᾽ αὑτό, where the fragment adduces αἴσθησις against the received axiom and where the Greek manuscripts split four ways (μὴ ἀεὶ Wimmer, μὴ δεῖ PJ, μὴ δὴ CA, καὶ ὡς δεῖ L) while Laks-Most read μὴ δεῖν on the Arabic's authority — et ut vid. Isḥāq — so that the Arabic breaks the tie at the axiom; (B) the first demand, μέχρι μὲν δὴ τούτων οἷον ἄρτιος ὁ λόγος … τὸ δὲ μετὰ ταῦτ᾽ ἤδη λόγου δεῖται πλείονος, a prior account marked complete to a point and the next question named; (C) the third demand and the method refused, τὸ δὲ κατὰ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν σφαιρῶν τῆς αἰτίας μείζονα ζητεῖ λόγον· οὐ γὰρ ὅ γε τῶν ἀστρολόγων, against Λ 8's derivation of the number of the spheres from Eudoxus and Callippus; (D) the landing, εὐλογώτερον οὖν εἶναί τινα συναφὴν καὶ μὴ ἐπεισοδιῶδες τὸ πᾶν, against Λ 10's ἐπεισοδιώδη τὴν τοῦ παντὸς οὐσίαν ποιοῦσιν at 1076 a 1 — the word van Raalte cites as a lexical parallel and which the edition prints as the place the aporiai arrive. The seat also records an editorial hazard found in the course of the work: the Greek Unicode range contains the koronis U+1FBD, so a tokenizer built on that range keeps elided forms as two-character tokens and any elision-normalization table silently fails to match them; a difference-of-centroids direction fitted on these two texts loaded entirely on δ᾽/ἀλλ᾽/δι᾽ against δέ/ἀλλά — on edition, not on voice — until it was caught. The plan of the edition is carried in the body: what it is, why an edition and not a paper, the four openings, text and apparatus policy, commentary policy, the two outstanding acquisitions (Alon 1985 for Isḥāq at the hinge lemmas; Gutas 2010 for the Arabic entire), the order of work, and what the edition would and would not settle.
